distinguishing_features: Injection is of alkaline scrubber slurry (CaCO/Ca(OH)2) at the duct-wall interface rather than a molybdate passivation inhibitor dosed into the absorber loop
Control is a wall-temperature/dew-point-crossover and interfacial-pH trigger rather than a low-temperature setpoint schedule for passive-film stability
Exploits neutralization chemistry and exothermic heat of neutralization to raise local wall temperature above the acid dew point
Uses existing FGD slurry and DCS pH/conductivity telemetry as the dosing driver
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Prevent formation of the corrosive acid-condensate layer on the carbon-steel duct wall by maintaining local interfacial pH and temperature above the acid dew point during gas cooling.
parsed.viable_reason: The stated heat balance is physically implausible: 142 kJ cannot raise ~100 m2 of duct wall by even 0.1 C (that needs MJ-scale energy), so the dew-point-suppression and 150 mV corrosion-drop claims cannot occur as written, and a 50 um slurry spray cannot maintain carbonate/bicarbonate surface pH at an impinging wall.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Dosing neutralizer at the duct wall tied to the dew-point crossover is a distinct mechanism not suggested by the absorber-loop passivation-inhibitor dosing of Prior Art 2, even though it is physically flawed.
